title: Normalize stacking behavior and rename semantic primitives for chart & table components
creator: Maya Chen
description: This ticket centralizes a set of surgical changes to the Figma component library focused on stacking rules (auto-layout axis and spacing behavior), semantic primitive renames for chart and table building blocks, and a publish gating checklist to avoid regressions. Goals: make instances resilient when nested, reduce accidental spacing drift in responsive panels, and create a small migration plan for teams consuming chart/table primitives.
acceptance_criteria: All chart/table primitives (GridCell, ChartAxis, LegendBlock, DataRow) renamed to agreed semantic tokens and documented in the token migration doc
Auto-layout direction/spacing conventions applied to 95% of library instances flagged during the audit; remaining exceptions have documented reason and tickets
Publish checklist added to the Figma library CI page and reviewed by PM/Engineering
Backfill script created (Figma API) to rename instances where possible and report manual-review candidates
No visual regressions in the core analytics dashboard after canary publish (validated by QA checklist)
steps: Audit: run instance inventory across 'Charts' and 'Tables' pages and export CSV of violations
Define conventions: axis-first stacking for charts (vertical axis container), row-first stacking for tables (horizontal cells), spacing tokens to use
Design rename map: map old primitive names to new semantic names and token keys
Prototype changes in a sandbox file and run quick QA on two representative pages (dashboard + reports)
Implement renames in the library file and run scripted instance backfill for straightforward matches
Create publish gating checklist and coordinate canary with product owners for smoke-testing
Merge notes into the Design System handbook and notify integrators via Slack + weekly digest
updates: 2025-11-10 - Created ticket. Initial audit exported: 412 instances across Charts/Tables. Major offenders: inconsistent cell padding, mixed stacking axis in Legend components.
2025-11-11 - Sync with Research: confirmed two screen sizes (desktop/compact) used by 87% of analytics consumers. Decided to standardize on 'compact' cell spacing token for small breakpoint.
2025-11-12 - Prototype completed in sandbox 'Charts-Tables-Sandbox'. Early feedback from Eng: prefer 'AxisRail' over 'ChartAxis' to avoid collisions with runtime naming.

2025-11-13 - Backfill script PoC finished (Python + Figma API). Script safely renames 278 instances and outputs 134 candidates for manual review. Created GH gist and linked in ticket. Beginning manual review with design interns.
2025-11-13 - Noted risk: three table variants are used in older marketing pages that cannot be auto-renamed (instances are flattened). Filed sub-issues and added to migration backlog.
risks: Auto-rename could break vendor integrations that reference instance names via tooling; mitigation: produce a mapping export and deprecation window
Flattened instances in marketing pages require manual effort and coordination with content owners
Small visual regressions possible when changing spacing tokens; mitigation: canary publish and rollback plan
notes: Decision: use semantic primitive names that match DS token keys (e.g., token: spacing.table.cell.compact -> primitive: CellCompact)
Decision: keep legacy aliases for 6 weeks via temporary components named Legacy-* to ease migration
Follow-up: create a short tutorial for product teams showing how to replace legacy instances with new primitives
QA checklist: visual diff screenshots, token audit, interaction test for legend wrapping, verify text truncation rules
